title: EIP-8279: Block Access List Byte Floor
description: Meter EIP-7928 Block Access List bytes at runtime and fold them into the EIP-8131 transaction floor, capping worst-case block size.
author: Toni Wahrstätter (@nerolation)
bodyPreview: ## Abstract Meter the bytes execution adds to the [EIP-7928](./eip-7928.md) Block Access List in an explicit per-transaction counter, and fold that count, at 64 gas/byte, into the transaction's floor accumulator — checked at runtime before the BAL grows. With EIP-7928 BALs, an attacker can pack ~1.55 MiB into a 60M-gas block: 75% of gas on cold `SLOAD`s (32 BAL bytes per 2,100 gas) + 25% on calldata at 16 gas/byte. On top of [EIP-8131](./eip-8131.md)'s tx-content floor (same rate), transaction content plus metered BAL bytes are capped at `block_gas_limit / 64 ≈ 0.89 MiB`, a ~42% cut in worst-case payload at an unchanged gas limit (about 35% in RLP-encoded bytes), with a small fixed overhead per transaction on top. Neither EIP alone closes the bypass: 8131 does not price BAL bytes; 8279 reuses 8131's floor. On mainnet, the runtime part raises the cost of at most about 4% of transactions under Glamsterdam execution costs. ## Motivation Every node must be able to handle the largest block an attacker can build, not the average one. Lowering that worst case buys headroom, which can either be spent on throughput by raising the gas limit or kept as a buffer. Left unspent, it is a direct gain in robustness. [EIP-7623](./eip-7623.md) introduced a calldata floor to cap worst-case block size, and [EIP-7976](./eip-7976.md) raised it to 64 gas per calldata byte. [EIP-7981](./eip-7981.md) extended that to access-list entries, and [EIP-8131](./eip-8131.md) generalises the floor to a uniform per-byte rule over all tx-content fields, including [EIP-7702](./eip-7702.md) authorization tuples and [EIP-4844](./eip-4844.md) blob versioned hashes. [EIP-7928](./eip-7928.md) introduces a new source of block bytes, the BAL, populated by runtime opcodes. None of those static floors cover it. The cheapest BAL contributor is a cold `SLOAD`: 32 bytes for 2,100 gas. Combined with all-non-zero calldata, an attacker lets cold `SLOAD`s raise execution gas up to the calldata floor, so the floor never adds anything: the calldata effectively costs its 16 gas/byte intrinsic rate, and the `SLOAD` keys fill the rest of the block. At a 60M gas limit: | Attack | Worst-case block bytes | |---|---| | Pure calldata at floor | 0.894 MiB (target) | | Cold-`SLOAD` bypass under EIP-7928 | **1.546 MiB** | `SSTORE`, address access, `CREATE`, and successful EIP-7702 delegations give further vectors. This EIP closes them with one uniform mechanism. ## Specification The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174). ### Constants ``` FLOOR_GAS_PER_BYTE = 64 # per-byte floor rate (EIP-7976) TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT = 16_777_216 # per-transaction execution-gas cap (EIP-7825) BAL_BYTES_PER_ADDRESS = 20 BAL_BYTES_PER_STORAGE_KEY = 32 BAL_BYTES_PER_STORAGE_VALUE = 32 BAL_BYTES_PER_BALANCE = 32 BAL_BYTES_PER_NONCE = 8 DELEGATION_CODE_BYTES = 23 # EIP-7702 delegation marker length ``` ### Data meter and floor accumulator Clients keep two internal, per-transaction counters and three sets on the execution environment for the duration of the transaction: - `bal_data_bytes` — an explicit count of the bytes execution contributes to the BAL, - `floor_gas_used` — the floor accumulator, derived from the static seed plus the metered bytes, and - `metered_addresses` — the addresses whose 20-byte address has already been metered, - `metered_storage_keys` — the `(storage_address, key)` pairs whose 32-byte storage key has already been metered, and - `metered_storage_values` — the `(storage_address, key)` pairs whose 32-byte storage value has already been metered. None is part of the signed transaction, RLP-encoded, gossiped, or persisted; no new transaction field or type is introduced. `floor_gas_used` is seeded with the static floor (below), `bal_data_bytes = 0`, and all three sets empty. The counters and sets are extended at runtime. No gas is reserved or deducted from the execution budget; the derived floor is checked against the transaction's execution-gas budget, `execution_budget = min(tx.gas, TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT)`, only to ensure the user can pay it if it ends up binding. ``` def meter_bal_data(tx_env, num_bytes): new_bal_data_bytes = tx_env.bal_data_bytes + num_bytes new_floor = tx_env.static_floor + new_bal_data_bytes * FLOOR_GAS_PER_BYTE if new_floor > tx_env.execution_budget: # min(tx.gas, TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT) raise OutOfGasError tx_env.bal_data_bytes = new_bal_data_bytes tx_env.floor_gas_used = new_floor def meter_bal_address(tx_env, address): if address in tx_env.metered_addresses: return meter_bal_data(tx_env, BAL_BYTES_PER_ADDRESS) tx_env.metered_addresses.add(address) def meter_bal_storage_key(tx_env, storage_address, key): slot = (storage_address, key) if slot in tx_env.metered_storage_keys: return meter_bal_data(tx_env, BAL_BYTES_PER_STORAGE_KEY) tx_env.metered_storage_keys.add(slot) def meter_bal_storage_value(tx_env, storage_address, key): slot = (storage_address, key) if slot in tx_env.metered_storage_values: return meter_bal_data(tx_env, BAL_BYTES_PER_STORAGE_VALUE) tx_env.metered_storage_values.add(slot) ``` `meter_bal_data` MUST be called BEFORE the matching BAL insertion or state mutation, and after the pre-state execution-gas validation that [EIP-7928](./eip-7928.md) requires for that access has passed. An access that fails its pre-state validation meters nothing, and an `OutOfGasError` at the metering step aborts before any unpaid BAL byte exists. The metered count is a deliberate upper bound on the transaction's actual BAL contribution (see [Reverts](#reverts) and [Repeated writes to the same slot](#repeated-writes-to-the-same-slot)); over-counting only raises the floor, never lowers it, so the bound below is never violated. ### Static floor seed The tx-content portion of the floor (calldata,
